newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN STOCKS TO WATCH TODAY - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN STOCKS TO WATCH TODAY - AUG 11.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$16.99 (-0.45)

Investors are expected on Monday to further punish Australian resources giant The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) for a management crisis that sent its stock tumbling last week. BHP managing director John Prescott said on Sunday that last week's resignation of three executives had created some short-term difficulties for the group Prescott said some tough decisions would have to be made to improve the performance of the company's existing assets as well as new projects. On Friday, BHP announced that its petroleum division chief, John O'Connor, had resigned due to irreconcilable differences with the board. The resignation compounded market concern after the sudden departures of minerals division chief Dick Carter and iron ore head Geoff Wedlock during the previous two days.

Australian beer and cigarette manufacturers were seeking urgent meetings with the government on Friday amid confusion about proposed tax changes which threaten to push up prices. Two of Australia's big three cigarette manufacturers, Philip Morris Cos Inc's Australian unit and W.D. & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd, have suspended deliveries.

The antitrust division of the U.S. Justice Department raised no objections to News Corp Ltd's acquisition of Heritage Media Corp, News said on Friday. Also J.P. Morgan Securities said Friday that analyst Matthew Harrigan started coverage of News Corp with a buy rating. Estimates for fiscal 1997 earnings were put at $1.28 per share and 1998 earnings at $1.24 per share. "A fair 9.0 times EBITDA multiple and at-cost valuations for News' gaggle of startup businesses dictates 1998 price targets of $22.65 for the voting ordinary ARDs and $20.98 for the non-voting preferred ADRs," Harrigan said.
Pacific Dunlop's partner in Vision Cables Pty Ltd, U.S.-based Commscope Inc, said on Friday night Vision Cables had suspended operations and it may post an abnormal charge related to the suspension.

The Australian Gas Light Co (AGL) said on Friday it had restructured its management to reflect the move towards national open-access energy markets. The company's major business functions will be organised into an energy infrastructure group and an energy sales and marketing group, managing director Len Bleasel said.
